posts.name: McBehrer
posts.cooked:
Parse, Termi-Nation Absolute Zero, Termi-Nation Unity, and Termi-Nation Bunker vs. Deadline in Freedom Tower.

I have to say, this was one of the easiest Mints I’ve gotten in a while. I used Flash Forge to pull a Pylon and 2 Raptor Bots, then used Reconfigure to bring out Champion Bot. Then Mission Control brought out the third Raptor, so when I played the rest on my next turn I dealt 18 damage. It all just kind of went downhill from there.

posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Mint.

 

Deadline: Termni-Nated.

 

Most fun/ironic part was when Absolute Zero blew up his Cryo Chamber when Frost's Cryo Chamber was also in play. "I just destroyed this chamber, what is it still doing here?" 

Oddly enough, it was Frost's Cryo Chamber that dealt the final damage to Deadline on the next environment turn!

posts.cooked:
this ended up being a nasty fight. 

AZ was down and out, but gave Deadline a bit of frostbite before sucuumbing to the heat of the battle. Unity was down to 1 HP, parse at 3, Bunker was the healthiest at 6.

i made a good handful of mistakes, upto and including forgetting that if something causes a AoE damage to be destroyed part-way through, the effect ends immedietely. 

Minted it, though it was a tough battle. Cryo-Bot dealt the final damage, Deadline apparently making the mistake of attacking it thinking Absolute Zero didn't go down(or at least that's how it's playing out in my head, thus making it MORE hilarious!)

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked: Trivial Mint.  Buffer Overflow is nice to deal with those indestructible devices, and there's plenty of control to get rid of unwanted Catastrophes and Entry Points.  One of the few villains against whom T-N AZ's power is an extremely safe bet, even though his modules came out very late, and indeed he ended up doing the lion's share of the damage.  Bunker... yeah, he just continues to be unimpressive.
